Charter

What neon1 is for, who it serves first, the values it works by, and what it leaves to others.

neon1 is a one-person technology practice in New York, run by me, Pradeep. neon1 LLC, formed in New York on July 24, 2025, is the company, and neon1 is the name it does business under. This charter is the short version of why it exists and how it behaves. Everything on the How I work shelf follows from it.

Mission

Help people and small organizations make their technology work together, improve everyday work, and keep the understanding and control to run what they own.

How

Cloud and AI native software, infrastructure, and connected devices, used where they make the result better. Every engagement ends in one of seven outcomes for each tool or system involved:

OutcomeWhat it means
KeepIt works. Leave it alone, maybe with a note on how it's used
ConfigureThe tool you have can already do it. Turn on what's there
IntegrateTwo tools that should talk to each other start talking
MigrateMove it somewhere that fits better, with your data intact
ReplaceSwap it for something that does the job with less effort
RetireStop paying for it and shut it down cleanly
OutsourceSomeone else is better placed to run it, and I'll say so

Moving everything to the cloud, or to an AI model, is never the default answer.

Values, as behavior

  • Listen first. I write down the real workflow before proposing anything.
  • Simplicity. I pick the option with the smallest ongoing burden that still meets the need.
  • Quality. The result works, can be recovered when it breaks, and you can run it.
  • Transparency. Scope, price, evidence, and limits are clear before work starts.
  • Your independence. You own your accounts and billing. You get the docs, the exports, and a clean way out.
  • Reuse before building. Existing tools and open-source software come first. I build only the part nothing else covers.

Who I serve first

  1. Owner-operated service businesses and small practices losing time between email, spreadsheets, point of sale, documents, and apps that don't talk to each other.
  2. Technical small businesses that need clarity on their cloud accounts, repeatable deployments, and recovery.
  3. Individuals, homes, and connected devices, when the travel, safety, and upkeep make sense.

What I refer to others

Some work deserves a specialist or a team with round-the-clock coverage. I'll point you to one rather than stretch:

  • 24/7 emergency support
  • Safety-critical equipment
  • Regulated professional judgment, such as legal, medical, or accounting advice
  • Large migrations that need a team
  • Formal security assurance, such as a penetration test or an audit opinion

Free help

Paid work is paid. Separately, I set aside a little time each month for community help, chosen at my discretion. That's a habit, not a claim to be a nonprofit.

Products

neon1 also builds tools: 1NEON, the client workspace, plus open-source projects such as AWS CLIP, DeployOps, and Ready, Secure, Go. They're shown as open source or in development, never sold as a service until they can be supported like one.

Related companies

N1 Supply LLC is a separate company for product experiments. It shares an owner with neon1 LLC but not its money, contracts, or intellectual property, unless a written agreement says otherwise.

Signature lines

1 is glad to be of service (from Bicentennial Man) and 1withtechnology. They say something about personality. They don't describe a scope of service.
